correctness.rationale: The projective degree is the top self-intersection of the Segre hyperplane class \(H=\sum_i h_i\), giving exactly \(N!/\prod_i a_i!\). The topological Euler characteristic is exactly \(\prod_i(a_i+1)\). Their quotient has the exact coordinate ratio \((N+1)/(a_j+2)=1+(\sum_{i\ne j}a_i-1)/(a_j+2)\). This is strictly greater than one for every coordinate move when there are at least three factors; for two factors the only flat direction occurs when the other dimension is one. The stated low-dimensional base cases therefore exhaust all possibilities. The bundled checker independently enumerates a broad finite grid and replays the ratio identity, but finite computation is not used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Projective degree and Euler characteristic are two canonical complexities of the same Segre variety: the first counts generic complementary linear intersections and the second counts the product cell structure. The result gives a complete phase diagram across every number of factors and all positive factor dimensions, with exactly two equality formats. The coordinate-growth identity explains the global transition structurally rather than by case enumeration, making the classification a reusable benchmark for product embeddings.
